nodes.label: Consent-Gated Evidence (requires_consent / consent_basis)
nodes.rationale: Each capture carries its own consent basis rather than inheriting one for the whole session: 'NaC application authorization' for network-side status reads, 'NaC authorization / end-user consent' for anything that discloses the subscriber's own identity or position. Number verification and step-up return CONSENT_REQUIRED as an INFO result, not a failure, so withheld consent never reads as adverse evidence.

nodes.label: Normalized Evidence Envelope (result/signal/detail/source/consent)
nodes.rationale: Every provider action, whether it made a real Nokia NaC round-trip or short-circuited, is flattened into the identical shape: result (PASS/FLAG/INFO), signal, detail, source, requires_consent, consent_basis. A uniform envelope lets the decision layer treat an unavailable adapter and a completed call as the same kind of fact rather than as an error path, which is what makes EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE expressible instead of thrown.

nodes.rationale: The same signal that catches an account takeover is the signal a stolen-and-replaced SIM produces. Measured, not estimated: a rules engine rejects 7 of 12, a scoring model that counts a missing check against you rejects all 12, the evidence-selecting agent rejects none at half the network spend. Reproducible via scripts/false_decline_baseline.py.

nodes.label: Ed25519-Signed Verdict Chain and Public Receipt
nodes.norm_label: ed25519-signed verdict chain and public receipt
nodes.rationale: Every verdict is signed and published at /r/<chain id> so the merchant, the customer and a dispute team can each verify it independently in a browser; altering one byte of one evidence detail breaks the signature. The point is that no party has to trust the issuer.

nodes.label: Hard-Coded Render Provenance (no runtime app calls)
nodes.norm_label: hard-coded render provenance (no runtime app calls)
nodes.rationale: The render talks to nothing at runtime: chain data, latencies, signature and public key were read out of isnad.db and docs/nac/*.json and frozen into timeline.js. That makes the cut reproducible frame-for-frame, at the cost of a provenance table that must be kept honest — scripted links are never presented as live network evidence.

nodes.label: Narration-Anchored Beat Grammar (s5b+1.2, s5b@0.55, s5b$0.4)
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the render is scheduled at an absolute second; every beat is expressed relative to the narration line it belongs to. A new voice, a different speed or a reworded line re-times the whole video off timings.json with nothing to re-tune by hand.

nodes.label: Budget-Bounded Early Stopping
nodes.rationale: The agent forms a hypothesis, buys the cheapest check that could settle it, and stops the moment the answer is decided — which is where the 50% call saving comes from. The admitted cost: a check it never bought cannot change its mind, so in 16 cases with a second adverse signal behind the stop point it allows 8. Framed as a dial, not a defect: policy.corroborate_before_allow = true takes it from 8 to 1.

nodes.label: Unknown Is Not Adverse
nodes.rationale: "We couldn't check" and "the check failed" are different facts. A withheld consent or an operator that has not enabled the API produces EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE / CONSENT_REQUIRED, and scoring that against the customer is what turns a lost phone into a week of declines. The whole engine is built on refusing to collapse the two.

nodes.label: Inlined QR Codes for Zero External Origins
nodes.norm_label: inlined qr codes for zero external origins
nodes.rationale: segno is pure Python with no runtime dependencies and the receipt QR SVG is inlined rather than fetched, so the public receipt console keeps zero external origins.

nodes.label: Nokia Network as Code (NaC)
nodes.rationale: The Apache-2.0 Python SDK through which every CAMARA call is made; Number Verification uses the documented authorization-code consent flow with a single-use token.

nodes.label: NaC integration — observed, not assumed
nodes.rationale: Five CAMARA APIs returned real responses (346–863 ms, median ~438 ms) recorded verbatim with SDK version and UTC timestamp and device identifier redacted; too few samples for a p95, which is therefore not claimed. Number Verification, step-up and Device Intelligence stay in the unverified list rather than being quietly promoted. The normalisation was written before any response was seen and the recordings confirmed it.

nodes.label: T1 — observed CAMARA responses
nodes.rationale: Every entry is one real, billable call, appended by scripts/t1_probe.py. Anything about NaC not in this file is explicitly an assumption.

nodes.label: Pinned Runtime Closure (requirements.lock.txt)
nodes.rationale: Generated from a clean venv holding requirements.txt and nothing else, so it is the runtime closure rather than a developer machine. The Dockerfile installs from here, which makes the image on demo morning the same image that was tested — unpinned '>=' had previously resolved to whatever was newest that day, and that is how the audited tree drifted out from under its own audit.

nodes.label: network-as-code pip==25.3 Packaging Defect
nodes.rationale: network-as-code 10.0.0 declares pip==25.3 as a hard runtime dependency, which is a vendor packaging mistake — the SDK never imports pip (occurrences are an error string, the README and a test) and resolves NetworkAsCodeApi with pip absent, verified rather than assumed. pip 25.3 carries six advisories, so pip is deliberately excluded from the lock file, stripped from the venv in the Dockerfile, and upgraded past 26.2 in CI before the audit step.

nodes.label: No-Op `nac` Optional Extra
nodes.rationale: The CAMARA provider was promoted to a core runtime dependency, so the `nac` extra is retained as an empty list purely for compatibility: `pip install .` and the Docker image then have the same dependency contract, and no install path can silently produce a build without the provider.

nodes.label: Dependency-Free Gemini Planner Adapter
nodes.rationale: The optional LLM planner (ISNAD_PLANNER=llm) calls Gemini over the existing httpx dependency instead of a vendor SDK, so a missing or unresolvable SDK cannot silently downgrade the demo to greedy-only planning.

nodes.label: Explicit Starlette Pin
nodes.rationale: Starlette is not a direct import, but it is FastAPI's ASGI layer and the subject of three reachable advisories (Host header, URL reconstruction, urlencoded-body DoS). Pinning it explicitly stops a FastAPI resolution from quietly dragging it backwards.

nodes.label: console.html — live agent console
nodes.rationale: Single file with zero external origins — no CDN, font host or analytics — because a demo venue may be locked down or offline.

nodes.label: judge.html — Judge Mode verified checkout
nodes.rationale: The 90-second presenter surface: checkout, evidence trace with provenance badges, signed receipt, and the simulator-only revocation beat.

nodes.label: receipt.html — public evidence receipt
nodes.rationale: Public, read-only and PII-free; verifies the Ed25519 signature client-side with WebCrypto and no external library.

nodes.label: Trust with a TTL (session revocation)
nodes.rationale: Answers the hardest anticipated judge question — 'what if the fraud happens after your check?' — by subscribing to the underlying signals for the session and revoking live when the SIM or device changes.

nodes.label: Video script — rendered cut and live take
nodes.norm_label: video script — rendered cut and live take
nodes.rationale: Each beat is anchored to a narration line rather than a hardcoded second, so changing voice, speed or wording re-times the whole render from timings.json.

nodes.label: Recover on camera rather than retake
nodes.norm_label: recover on camera rather than retake
nodes.rationale: A live link timing out, the planner falling back to greedy, or an expired console token are all scripted as things to narrate: a recovered failure is better footage than a retake, and the organisers' own guide says agents that gracefully degrade demo much better.

nodes.label: The one seam named out loud in the render
nodes.norm_label: the one seam named out loud in the render
nodes.rationale: The live NaC rows in the rendered cut are real responses captured on 30 Aug and replayed, not calls made while the frames were drawn — so the narration says 'that's a real Nokia Network as Code call', which is true of the response on screen, and never says 'just now'.

nodes.label: Decision thresholds (allow_below / decline_above)
nodes.rationale: The shipped 0.15 allow_below is a dial, not a defect: tightening it to 0.05 cuts corroborated-adverse allows from 8/16 to 1/16 at 142 checks instead of 96, but makes ATTESTED_PARTIAL unreachable in the demo, and a grade nothing can produce is worse than a dial nobody moved.

nodes.label: CAMARA — open network API standard
nodes.rationale: The first time operator-held truth about a physical SIM in radio range of a physical tower became programmable by third parties — the one proof generative AI has not broken.

nodes.label: Cash-on-delivery fraud as the market wedge
nodes.norm_label: cash-on-delivery fraud as the market wedge
nodes.rationale: COD orders carry far higher rejection rates because there is no verified buyer commitment at checkout, making refused deliveries a concrete cost line to lead with. Priced per verification against the cost of one wasted delivery run — usage-based revenue rather than a ministry-sales model.

nodes.label: Isnad — the hadith chain of transmission
nodes.norm_label: isnad — the hadith chain of transmission
nodes.rationale: A thousand-year-old methodology for evaluating a report by scrutinising every transmitter in its chain. The product reproduces the structure literally — the chain is the UX and the audit model, not only a metaphor — and it gives MENA judges a cultural hook a generic fraud-detection pitch cannot.

nodes.label: GSMA MENA Ignite / Open Gateway Hackathon 2026
nodes.norm_label: gsma mena ignite / open gateway hackathon 2026
nodes.rationale: Requires CAMARA calls to be agent-initiated decision inputs, not user-triggered buttons — which is why the choice of the next API is itself the deliverable. Judges penalise submissions that try to do everything, so Tier 1 is built and Tier 2/3 stay roadmap slides.

nodes.label: Reverse Isnad — verifying the caller to the customer
nodes.norm_label: reverse isnad — verifying the caller to the customer
nodes.rationale: Flips the direction of verification to target vishing and impersonation — a scam type virtually every judge has personally experienced — while reusing the same APIs and the same engine.

nodes.label: Tazkiya (تزكية) — human vouching
nodes.rationale: Roadmap-only Tier 3: strengthens a thin-file chain with a vouch from an employer or long-tenured relative, extending the financial-inclusion story using the region's own historical mechanism.

nodes.label: Wakala (وكالة) — agent delegation
nodes.rationale: Roadmap-only Tier 3: a scoped, expiring, spend-limited mandate chaining every AI-agent action back to a verified human SIM, turning the agent-economy pitch into a named, culturally grounded product.

nodes.label: Isnad mentorship brief (one-pager)
nodes.rationale: One page so the 30 minutes do not go on background; carries three already-measured decisions to be stress-tested rather than a request for a code review.

nodes.label: Mentorship outreach email (stc)
nodes.rationale: Each question states a decision already made and asks the mentor to find the flaw; open-ended 'any feedback?' requests are deprioritised by the programme guide.

nodes.label: Demo/production parity — only the provider differs
nodes.norm_label: demo/production parity — only the provider differs
nodes.rationale: The stage demo calls the same endpoint and the same agent loop as production, with only ISNAD_PROVIDER changed, so judges watch the real decision engine reason rather than a scripted animation.

nodes.label: privacy.html — what we keep
nodes.rationale: Holds no numbers of its own; every figure is read live from /v1/privacy/posture so the disclosure page cannot drift from the running settings.

nodes.label: EvidenceProvider adapter contract
nodes.rationale: One Protocol so the agent never knows whether it is talking to the network or a mock; each method returns a normalized EvidenceLink rather than the raw CAMARA payload, so no coordinates or MSISDN metadata leak upstream.

nodes.label: Part 4 pre-deployment hardening gate
nodes.rationale: Run against the container on a fresh volume with demo_mode false: no demo key in the console, anonymous verify 401, docs endpoints 404, cross-tenant chain reads 404, and a chain that still verifies after the container is destroyed and recreated on the same volume.

nodes.label: T3 — rebuild the planner so the agent actually reasons
nodes.norm_label: t3 — rebuild the planner so the agent actually reasons
nodes.rationale: The hardcoded rationale string in _selection_event dressed a heuristic up as reasoning, and a judge who opens the repo mid-demo finds that in ninety seconds. STOP becomes a first-class action, the rationale is the model's own sentence, a hard call ceiling caps spend, and greedy stays a visible fallback — framed as reliability engineering rather than hidden as a bluff.

nodes.label: S14 — committed secrets in .env.bak
nodes.rationale: .gitignore listed .env as an exact name so an editor's .env.bak-* did not match; two prior audits missed it. Not pushed, but still in local history and the repo lived inside iCloud Drive, so rotation is the only action that closes it. Filed with a test that scans tracked files for credential patterns.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — graphify agent instructions
nodes.rationale: Tells any agent working the repo to query the knowledge graph before grepping, because a scoped subgraph is far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Phase 2 full audit (30 Aug 2026)
nodes.rationale: Audited against the runbook rather than against the runbook's own status table or the handoff, because those are the claims under audit; every finding cites a test name, file:line, commit or pasted output.

nodes.label: Runbook invariants (gather() seam, no raw signals, no logging)
nodes.norm_label: runbook invariants (gather() seam, no raw signals, no logging)
nodes.rationale: gather() is the only seam between agent and network so provider swaps touch nothing else; raw signals, coordinates and phone numbers are never persisted; consent tokens never leave process memory; the application has no logger at all; and any planner must be able to stop.

nodes.label: Prompt-injection boundary for the planner
nodes.rationale: link.detail carries operator-supplied strings on the NaC path and claimed_identity is 120 characters of caller-controlled text; either reaching the prompt is an indirect injection channel into the component that decides whether to trust someone. Pass enums, numbers and booleans only; validate the model's choice by exact equality; keep the narrative display-only.

nodes.label: policy.yaml — the single tuning surface
nodes.rationale: Costs, signal weights, thresholds and grading all live in one YAML file so tuning never requires a code change; a new threshold belongs here, not in a constant.

nodes.label: registry.yaml — institution number registry
nodes.rationale: Answers the question no CAMARA API can — which institution a published number belongs to. The network attests the line; the registry attests the name on it.

nodes.label: Evidence budget and cheapest-evidence-first
nodes.rationale: cost is normalized spend (latency + money + friction), not dollars; the agent stops as soon as belief is decisive, which is why a clean chain often costs one call instead of six — and why an unbought signal cannot move a verdict.

nodes.label: corroboration: SIM_SWAPPED → [device_swap, location_verify]
nodes.rationale: The same handset still at the usual place is a customer who lost a phone and replaced the SIM, not a takeover. If the budget cannot cover the exculpatory checks the decline stands rather than looping. Action names resolve to the Action enum at load so a typo fails loud.

nodes.label: grading.min_network_links_for_allow
nodes.rationale: The mirror of corroboration on the decline side: one link is not a chain, whichever way it points. Applies only when local evidence is in the chain; a run decisive at the prior with nothing gathered stays a deliberate separate outcome.

nodes.label: OTP counterfactual pricing block
nodes.rationale: Every figure carries its source and a list_price/estimate tag; camara_call_usd and false_decline_cost_usd are null on purpose because no defensible public figure exists (NaC is contract-priced, false-decline cost is merchant-specific). A figure a judge can check and finds invented is worse than no figure. The drop-off source's conflict of interest is recorded in the file.

nodes.label: Signal → log-odds vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Weights came from reasoning and simulator responses, not from watching real traffic — a recent SIM swap (+2.2) moves belief further than a device change (+1.6), and an unavailable check moves it not at all (0.0). Named as the weakest-grounded part of the design in the mentor questions.

nodes.label: Caller velocity — the cross-subscriber signal
nodes.rationale: One number screened against many people in a short window: no individual call in a campaign looks wrong, the pattern does. The only signal no per-call check can produce, and the only one that improves as more people use the system. Both tuning numbers are declared INVENTED for demo legibility, not derived from measured campaign traffic.

nodes.label: Inbound-only hotline as a spoof signal
nodes.norm_label: inbound-only hotline as a spoof signal
nodes.rationale: The institution publishes the number for customers to call IN and never originates from it, so seeing it as caller ID means it was spoofed — and a published number is a convenient thing to spoof precisely because customers recognise it.

nodes.label: gather.mode — sequential vs parallel
nodes.rationale: Cheapest-first-then-stop is what makes the cost story true. Parallel trades that for latency by paying for evidence the sequential path might never have needed, which directly weakens the OTP counterfactual. The speed story and the cost story pull against each other; opt in per request, never globally.

nodes.label: OTP_CONFIRMED — reserved, nothing emits it
nodes.rationale: An OTP is sent by the merchant in a channel this service does not own, so an OTP outcome could only arrive as a merchant-reported fact, never as evidence the agent gathered. Kept priced so the counterfactual has a number to argue against.

nodes.label: REGISTRY_MATCH_UNANNOUNCED = 0.0
nodes.rationale: Zero on purpose, and the most important line in the block: caller ID is spoofable, so a scammer presenting the bank's real number produces exactly this hit. Giving it a negative delta would build a machine that trusts the attacks it exists to catch. REGISTRY_UNLISTED is zero for the mirror reason — absence from a hand-curated registry is not evidence.

nodes.label: step_up_otp — priced, never selected
nodes.rationale: cheapest_stepup used to fall back to it, spending 6 of a 12 budget on a provider call that does not exist. CHALLENGE is itself the instruction to step the customer up; the merchant runs it.

nodes.label: Nothing in the registry is a real bank number
nodes.norm_label: nothing in the registry is a real bank number
nodes.rationale: Every shipped entry is marked demo_fixture so it cannot be mistaken for published fact; real entries need a real source URL and a human who checked it.

nodes.label: Registry provenance is mandatory (basis / source / verified_on)
nodes.norm_label: registry provenance is mandatory (basis / source / verified_on)
nodes.rationale: An entry asserts that a phone number belongs to a named bank, and an unsourced assertion of that kind is worse than no entry — a wrong entry is a way to get a scammer's number trusted. A missing field raises at load, not at lookup.
